findings.summary: The new command has no contract for the repository-mandated --json mode.
findings.evidence: docs/domain/platform/platform-context.md:49-50 and docs/guide/commands.md:6-11 say every command has --json and that stdout is one JSON document; the brief's S1 and S2 outputs (the worked examples at brief:204-229) pin text only and never say what --json emits.
findings.fix: Decide and pin the exact JSON success document for --check, no-op, install, and plugin outcomes, including the install target/current fields and nonfatal plugin failures; also state whether each failure emits an error object on stdout or only the existing one-line stderr error.

findings.summary: S2 treats both agents as if plugin-list success exposed vloop@vloop, but the binding contract says their identifiers differ.
findings.evidence: The new brief says at :94 and :148-150 that a list names vloop@vloop; the depended-on brief says at :299 that Claude counts id starting with vloop@, while at :341 Copilot counts name == vloop. internal/cli/doctor.go:809 and :857 implement those two distinct shapes.
findings.fix: State the literal predicate per agent: Claude entries with id vloop@vloop (or the intended starts-with rule), and Copilot entries with name vloop and marketplace vloop; repeat those JSON shapes in the worked example and gate them independently.

findings.summary: A plugin list command failure or invalid JSON has no specified result even though plugin failures are promised to be reported and nonfatal.
findings.evidence: Brief:83-85 promises that a plugin failure prints its reason, but :148-153 defines only successful list/no-plugin and update outcomes; internal/cli/doctor.go:774-785 shows plugin listing can fail either by process exit or JSON decode.
findings.fix: Pin one exact nonfatal line for list failure/invalid JSON (using the defined last or first output line), include it in the worked example, and make the S2 gate exercise each agent-list failure as well as update failure.

decisions: Tests fake go, claude and copilot with Go programs on PATH: appropriate and consistent with the Windows run and the no-real-tools constraint.
Semver comparison uses the existing golang.org/x/mod/semver dependency: appropriate; go.mod already contains golang.org/x/mod v0.37.0.
--check with --version compares the running module version with the requested target: appropriate and needed to make the combined flags deterministic.
